-- 096_candidate_disposition_exhausted.sql
--
-- A DISPOSITION FOR "EXHAUSTED -- GIVEN UP ON FOR NOW", BY OWNER RULING 2026-09-25.
--
-- The owner ruled on 2026-09-25: "if we can't access something from anywhere then we
-- have to give up on it for now." Batch 20 applied that to candidates 109 (Walter 1971)
-- and 110 (the 1957 Illinois dissertation) and had nowhere to put it: the column's CHECK
-- offered REHOME, MISCELLANEOUS, PENDING-VERIFICATION, OUT-OF-SCOPE and ADMITTED, so both
-- rows said "exhausted, not queued for anyone" in prose while their typed disposition,
-- PENDING-VERIFICATION, told every sweep and every reader to go and verify them. The
-- prose and the column disagreed, and only the column is joinable -- the shape rule 8
-- exists to prevent. An independent adversarial pass on batch 20 raised it (finding
-- #15); the owner ruled the same day that a real, CHECK-permitted value be added.
--
-- WHAT IT MEANS, stated once here because the CHECK cannot carry prose: the item is
-- identified, and NO ROUTE to its text exists from anywhere this project can reach. It is
-- not OUT-OF-SCOPE (the item is on-topic) and not PENDING-VERIFICATION (nothing is pending).
-- "For now" is the owner's word: the value records a decision that can be revisited, not
-- a finding about the item. It is NOT for an item behind a possibly-transient barrier
-- (a bot check, a Cloudflare interstitial) that an ordinary browser gets past -- batch 20
-- left candidate 123 PENDING-VERIFICATION on exactly that distinction.
--
-- WHY A TABLE REBUILD. SQLite cannot alter a CHECK in place. The DDL below is the live
-- CREATE statement with one value added, generated from sqlite_master rather than
-- retyped (the lesson of migrations 089/091), and the table stays STRICT. Every live
-- disposition is inside the new set, so nothing on disk is invalidated. No view, trigger
-- or foreign key refers to search_candidates (verified against sqlite_master before
-- writing); its two indexes are recreated verbatim.
--
-- Consumers read the vocabulary from this CHECK (dbcore.check_values), so add-candidate
-- and resolve-candidate accept EXHAUSTED the moment this applies; no list in code
-- changes.

CREATE TABLE search_candidates_new (
  candidate_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  exec_id          INTEGER REFERENCES search_executions(exec_id),  -- which search surfaced it
  found_under_slug TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES slugs(slug),  -- the slug being searched when it surfaced
  suggested_slug   TEXT REFERENCES slugs(slug),  -- best-fit slug; NULL = MISCELLANEOUS / undecided
  disposition      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (disposition IN
                     ('REHOME','MISCELLANEOUS','PENDING-VERIFICATION','OUT-OF-SCOPE','ADMITTED',
                      'EXHAUSTED')),
  title            TEXT NOT NULL,
  locator          TEXT,                 -- DOI / URL / PMID as retrieved
  locator_status   TEXT CHECK (locator_status IS NULL OR locator_status IN
                     ('UNVERIFIED','RESOLVED','DEAD')),
  tier_guess       INTEGER CHECK (tier_guess IS NULL OR tier_guess BETWEEN 1 AND 6),
  harm_finding     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (harm_finding IN (0,1)),
  why_not_admitted TEXT,                 -- required in practice: metadata gap, unverified, etc.
  notes            TEXT,
  created_by_session          TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at       TEXT NOT NULL
, resolved_ref_id TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id)) STRICT;

INSERT INTO search_candidates_new ("candidate_id", "exec_id", "found_under_slug", "suggested_slug", "disposition", "title", "locator", "locator_status", "tier_guess", "harm_finding", "why_not_admitted", "notes", "created_by_session", "created_at", "resolved_ref_id")
    SELECT "candidate_id", "exec_id", "found_under_slug", "suggested_slug", "disposition", "title", "locator", "locator_status", "tier_guess", "harm_finding", "why_not_admitted", "notes", "created_by_session", "created_at", "resolved_ref_id" FROM search_candidates;

DROP TABLE search_candidates;

ALTER TABLE search_candidates_new RENAME TO search_candidates;

CREATE INDEX ix_sc_suggested ON search_candidates(suggested_slug, disposition);
CREATE INDEX ix_sc_harm ON search_candidates(harm_finding);

Reviewed scripts/db.py diff (resolve-candidate --suggested-slug, link-admission, amend-population-match, amend-term, plus argparse wiring and dispatch) against the live schema and dbcore.py helpers.

No concrete bugs found in the categories requested (argument-order mismatches, refusal gaps, SQL/schema mismatches, stale sqlite3.Row reads, dry-run/correctness interactions, string-formatting errors).

Specifics checked and confirmed correct:
- Dispatch-to-function argument mapping is correct for all four commands (resolve_candidate, link_admission, amend_population_match, amend_term) — every dispatch call uses keyword args matching the parameter names exactly, so there's no positional/keyword mismatch even though resolve_candidate's signature gained a new trailing parameter.
- All new/changed SQL (`UPDATE search_candidates ... resolved_ref_id=COALESCE(?,...), suggested_slug=COALESCE(?,...)`, `INSERT INTO search_admissions`, `UPDATE search_executions SET findings_note=?`, `UPDATE evidence_population_match SET match_grade=?, mismatch_note=?`, `UPDATE terms SET definition=?, scope_note=?, updated_at=?, updated_by_session=?`) matches the live column names/order/nullability confirmed via `PRAGMA table_info` on data/guidebook.db, and matches migration 096's rebuilt `search_candidates` (which added `resolved_ref_id` and the `EXHAUSTED` disposition).
- `dbcore.connect()`'s dry_run handling executes the full function body (including every `raise Refusal`) and only differs at the very end (`commit()` vs `rollback()`); a raised Refusal always propagates via the `except Exception: rollback(); raise` path regardless of dry_run, so no refusal is ever skipped in --dry-run.
- Validation in all four functions happens entirely before any `conn.execute(UPDATE/INSERT ...)`, so there's no check-after-mutation ordering bug.
- Places that read a `sqlite3.Row` fetched before the UPDATE (`row["disposition"]`, `row["suggested_slug"]`, `row["match_grade"]`, `row[field]` in amend_term) are all read for "was"/trailer text — the Row object is never mutated in place (Rows are immutable, and the code builds a separate `new` dict), so these correctly report pre-update values rather than stale/already-mutated ones. Traced amend_term's two cases (amending "definition" vs amending "scope_note" itself) explicitly; both produce the intended final scope_note (new value + trailer quoting the old value).
- `dbcore.exists()`, `check_vocab()`, `fold_ref()` are called with correct argument order and against correct table/column names (`slugs.slug`, `evidence_sources.ref_id`, `evidence_population_match.match_grade`).
- `link_admission`'s three-part refusal chain (search exists → source exists → matching ADMITTED candidate exists → not already linked → no conflicting exec) requires all conditions before insert; the "already linked" case short-circuits with `changed: False` rather than re-raising, which is intentional idempotency, not a bug.

One low-confidence, non-blocking observation (not reported as a finding): `resolve_candidate`'s pre-existing (unmodified in this diff) `--admitted-ref-id` handling does not run the value through `dbcore.fold_ref()` before storing it in `resolved_ref_id`, while `link_admission` folds `--ref-id` to uppercase before comparing. In practice this can't actually diverge, because `resolve_candidate` also requires `admitted_ref_id` to exactly match an existing `evidence_sources.ref_id` (which is always canonical/uppercase) before it will write it — so a case-mismatched value would already be refused at write time, not silently stored. I checked this carefully and don't believe it's exploitable, so I'm not filing it as a finding.
